rapport_notes: Calvin is conversational, patient, and handles customer objections (cynicism about overages) with calm reassurance; tone is professional and friendly throughout.
process_discipline_notes: Calvin mentions 'discounts' and after-the-fact resolution twice (once when Patrick raises the overage concern, again when explaining estimate philosophy), creating redundancy without clean silence after open-ended questions.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: None — Calvin launches directly into probing ("you're moving . . . the nineteenth") without framing the call length or benefit of the questions.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Calvin goes straight into logistics (move date, packing vs. furniture, box counts, special items).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no customer concerns raised that required two-layer follow-up. Patrick volunteered one piece of information (bunk bed complexity), which Calvin resolved with one answer ("yes, disassemble reassembly included").
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with_answered_anywhere: "We will wrap all the furniture to prevent damages . . . we will have tools to do disassemble reassembly on things like the bed, Washer/Dryer." Covered as part of pricing/service description in Stage 3.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming_answered_anywhere: Not covered — no mention of who specifically will show up, crew lead name, or Meet Your Mover concept.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "For a two truck four man crew . . . I would probably put you with four guys for maybe around four and a half to six hours. So that would put us, let's see, see here with that hourly rate between about $1,728 and 2304 if it did take a full six hours." Anchored range + personalized to this customer's furniture load and crew size.
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: "The main thing though that would come into play is . . . there was no boxes for us to move . . . if you had even some pictures we could estimate it and be a lot like most accurate with our estimates." Acknowledges variability due to customer's information gaps.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: "Once we exceed the minimum, we would just bill in fifteen minute increments until the move was completed. So, you'll just pay for the time that you used this crew for basically."
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair_then_silence: Not asked in this form; the call transitions directly to the walkthrough scheduling.
evidence_quotes.close_explicit_ask: Not a traditional close — call ends with scheduling the walkthrough: "I'll send it over around 10:30 AM." No rate-lock or explicit "would you like our help" ask.

top_strength: Calvin expertly handles Patrick's objection about overage risk ("I don't wanna pay $900 for that") with acknowledgment, transparency about the discount review process, and reassurance without dodging the concern—building trust rather than pushing past it.
coaching_note: Never ask for the customer's agenda or frame the call with a quid pro quo—jump straight into logistics instead of discovery, and skip all Stage 2 differentiators (On-Time Guarantee, Communication, Meet Your Mover); route to walkthrough cleanly but miss the chance to earn trust and consent upfront.
